diagnostic_evidence.quote: v^{\varepsilon}(t,x,y,z) := (v \ast \zeta_{\varepsilon})(t,x,y,z) := \int_{-\varepsilon^{2}}^{0} \int_{|e| < \varepsilon} v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e) \, de \, d\tau,
It is clear that \( v^{\varepsilon} \in C_{b}^{\infty}\)

issues.failure_explanation: The kernel is defined on \(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^d\), but it is convolved with \(v:[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}^{3d}\to\mathbb{R}\), and the same \(e\in\mathbb{R}^d\) is subtracted from \(x,y,z\) simultaneously. The shift set is only the diagonal \(\{(e,e,e)\\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{3d}\), so transverse directions are not averaged. For example \(v(t,x,y,z)=|x-y|\) satisfies the stated Holder-Lipschitz condition, yet this convolution leaves \(x-y\) unchanged, so \(v^\varepsilon=v\notin C^1\). Thus the claimed smoothness and the derivative estimates for \(u^\varepsilon\) and \(u_h^\varepsilon\) are not established by the construction as written.

failure_location.quote: let \( \zeta \in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{d}) \) be a nonnegative mollifier with unit integral and compact support in \([-1,0] \times B_{1}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \(\zeta\) by a nonnegative \(C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{3d})\) mollifier supported in \([-1,0]\times B_1\), set \(\zeta_\varepsilon(\tau,e)=\varepsilon^{-(3d+2)}\zeta(\tau/\varepsilon^2,e/\varepsilon)\), and integrate over \(e\in\mathbb{R}^{3d}\) applied independently to \(x,y,z\); then keep the stated Krylov estimates with the corresponding \(K_\zeta\).
issues.overall_effect: The regularization used in (C2)-(C3), in the substitutions of \(u^\varepsilon\) and \(u_h^\varepsilon\) into the consistency lemma, and hence in the definitions of \(E_1,E_2\) and the error bounds of the main theorem and CLT rate theorems are unsupported until the mollifier is redefined on \(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{3d}\).
issues.title: Diagonal mollifier is not a mollifier on the full spatial domain
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained replacement of a standard construction and does not change the method, rates, or advertised scope, but the construction as written is invalid and every mollification-based estimate must be re-based on the corrected kernel.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
u_h(t,x,y,z) = \phi(x,y,z), \quad \text{in } [0,h) \times \mathbb{R}^{3d}, \\
 u_h(t,x,y,z) = \mathbb{\hat{E}} \left[ u_h(t-h, x + h^{1/2} X, y + h Y, z + h^{1/\alpha} Z) \right], \quad \text{in } [h,1] \times \mathbb{R}^{3d}.

issues.failure_explanation: The scheme is piecewise constant in time on intervals \([kh,(k+1)h)\), with jumps of order \(h^{1/2}\) at grid points. If \(\varepsilon^2<h\), a future time mollification centered within \(\varepsilon^2\) below a grid point still averages across that jump, producing an \(O(h^{1/2})\) error even when \(\varepsilon\ll h^{1/2}\). Hence \(\|u_h-u_h^\varepsilon\|_\infty\le 2C_0\varepsilon\) is not implied by Lemma uh_regularity, whose estimate contains the additional \(h^{1/2}\) term.

failure_location.quote:
\[
\|u_h - u_h^{\varepsilon}\|_{\infty} \leq 2C_0 \varepsilon, \quad
\|\partial_t;l D_x^k u_h^{\varepsilon}\|_{\infty} \leq 2C_0 K_{\zeta} (\varepsilon + h^{1/2}) \varepsilon^{-2l-k}, \quad \forall k,l \in \mathbb{N}.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use \(\|u_h-u_h^\varepsilon\|_\infty\le 2C_0(\varepsilon+h^{1/2})\), or prove that the minimization over \(\varepsilon\) may be restricted to \(\varepsilon\ge h^{1/2}\), and adjust the lower-bound \(h^{1/2}\) coefficient accordingly. In the later optimization \(\gamma<1/2\), so \(h^{1/2}=o(\varepsilon)\) and the displayed rate survives.
issues.overall_effect: The lower-bound half of the main theorem uses an unjustified replacement of \(u_h^\varepsilon\) by \(u_h\); consequently the stated lower constant and the two-sided CLT/example rate bounds are not proved in the displayed form.
issues.title: Uniform error of the time-mollified scheme omits the h^{1/2} jump term
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and preserves the \(h^{1/2}\) boundary term, the consistency term, the optimized rate, and the advertised scope; only an explicit lower-bound constant needs to be enlarged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, for sufficiently small \( h > 0 \), we have:
Setting \( h = \frac{1}{n} \) and \( (t,x,y,z) = (1,0,0,0) \), it follows from Theorem \ref{main theorem} that

issues.failure_explanation: The proof explicitly sets \(h=1/n\) and invokes the main theorem, but that theorem is only asserted for sufficiently small \(h>0\). The CLT statement nevertheless claims the two-sided bound for every \(n\in\mathbb{N}\). For the finitely many large-\(h\) cases, including \(h=1\), the bound is not derived; moreover it cannot be uniform in all \(\phi\) with the stated constant data because the left side may be as large as \(2\|\phi\|_\infty\) while \(C_0\) does not control \(\|\phi\|_\infty\).

failure_location.quote: for all \( n \in \mathbb{N} \), where the functions \( E_1 \) and \( E_2 \) are defined in Theorem \ref{main theorem}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the conclusion for all sufficiently large \(n\) (equivalently sufficiently small \(h\)), or enlarge the constant to depend also on \(\|\phi\|_\infty\) so that finitely many exceptional \(n\) are absorbed.
issues.overall_effect: The asymptotic Berry-Esseen-type statement remains intact, but the universal finite-\(n\) guarantee is stronger than what the small-\(h\) scheme theorem supports.
issues.title: CLT rate theorem is quantified for all n although the scheme theorem requires small h
issues.why_classification: The repair only restricts the quantifier or adds a finite-\(n\) constant; the convergence rate, two-sided bound, and main asymptotic claim are unchanged.
